indicator_definition: The under-five mortality rate is the probability that a child born in a given year will die before reaching the age of five, expressed per 1,000 live births. It reflects the cumulative effect of multiple determinants of child survival including nutrition, healthcare access, sanitation and living conditions. Data are compiled from national vital statistics.
rationale: Reducing child mortality is a fundamental measure of human development and of the effectiveness of health and social systems. High under-five mortality rates reflect inadequate healthcare access and poor living conditions. Progress means a steady reduction in preventable deaths among children under five.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled from national civil registration and vital statistics systems. The rate is calculated from age-specific death rates for children under five. Eurostat compiles and validates data from national statistical authorities following harmonised definitions.
